chunks: Hariz narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

“It was found on a stone: ‘Indeed, I am Allah, the Lord of Bakkah. I made it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, and on the day I created the sun and the moon. I surrounded it with seven angels, a blessed surrounding for its people in water and milk. Its provision comes to it from routes above it, below it, and through the mountain pass.’”

key_terms.أَمْلَاكٍ: angels surrounding and guarding the sanctuary
key_terms.الثَّنِيَّةِ: the mountain pass or elevated route
key_terms.بَكَّةَ: Bakkah, the sacred sanctuary of Makkah
key_terms.رِزْقُهَا: its sustenance and provision granted by Allah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the divine origin and blessings of Bakkah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes an inscription declaring that Allah created Bakkah and blessed it from the earliest act of creation. It emphasizes the sacred status of the sanctuary, its divine protection, and the special provision granted to its people.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2311 - Hariz narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"It was found inscribed on a stone: 'I am Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of Bakkah. I created it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, the day I created the sun and the moon. I surrounded it with seven blessed angels, a sanctuary blessed for its people with water and milk. Its sustenance comes to it from paths above and below and through the mountain passes.'"
